rv.q: In the two decades since its Public Theater debut, Suzan-Lori Parks's Venus has lost none of its power to unsettle and appall. If anything, the story of Saartjie Baartman's exploitation at the hands of early-19th-century human traffickers—some venal, some high-minded—has gained in shock value.

"'Venus' is pageant-like, intellectual and reminiscent of 'The Elephant Man.' And now Lear deBessonet has staged an excellent revival of the play...Whether the play’s bold and self-aware theatricality adds to or detracts from the impact of the storytelling is up for debate.
